newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Menem to sign health fund decree - paper.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem to sign health fund decree - paper.

text.p: Argentina's President Carlos Menem will Monday sign a controversial decree to allow competition within the $2.5-billion union health fund business, the La Nacion daily reported Saturday.

Unions have threatened a 48-hour general strike if Menem goes ahead with the decree, which they say is the first step towards leaving poorer workers without health coverage. Unions also fear eventual competition with private health funds, which could deprive them of a major source of revenue.
The decree would allow workers to choose between different unions' funds as of April 1, said La Nacion.

Argentine law obliges all workers to pay into their union's health plan. But the poor service offered by most union health plans means that many firms also contract private health funds for their employees, meaning a double cost.

Menem's plan will not at first establish free competition between the union health funds and the private funds, as it will only allow workers to shift between union plans. The government plans total competition with private funds to begin in 1998.
